findings.failure_mode: Missing file, permission denied, or path length exhaustion aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, std::io::Error> and propagate with ? or handle with map_err

findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV value (non-numeric, empty, or overflows) causes a panic instead of a typed parse error
findings.fix: Return Result and use .parse::<u16>()? or .parse::<u32>().map_err() with a domain parse error, remove the cast

findings.problem: Lossy as cast from u32 to u16: .parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16
findings.failure_mode: Values in range 256..=u32::MAX silently truncate to u16, violating domain invariants without any error signal
findings.fix: Parse directly as u16 with .parse::<u16>()?, or use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err() and return a typed overflow error

findings.problem: split(',') + collect() + indexed access instead of split_once
findings.failure_mode: Allocates a full Vec for every line when only two fields are needed; allocates unnecessarily and invites index-out-of-bounds on malformed lines
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to get (name_str, rest), then parse rest from the second field

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing parts[0] and parts[1] panics on short lines
findings.failure_mode: A line with fewer than 2 commas (e.g., empty line or single field) causes an index-out-of-bounds panic
findings.fix: Use split_once and match on the Option<(str, str)> result; return a typed parse error instead of panicking

findings.failure_mode: I/O (stdout) is embedded in what should be a pure parsing function, making the core impure and untestable; log output cannot be suppressed in tests or controlled by the caller
findings.fix: Remove println! from the core; if logging is needed, pass a callback or use a logging abstraction at the shell boundary

findings.problem: load_sessions mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing logic in a single function returning concrete Vec
findings.failure_mode: Cannot unit-test the parsing logic without mocking the filesystem; no separation between shell (I/O) and core (parsing)
findings.fix: Split into load_sessions_raw(path) -> Result<String, io::Error> at the shell boundary, and parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> in the pure core

findings.problem: Record.name is a raw String with no domain validation
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, whitespace-only names, or other invalid names are accepted by construction
findings.fix: Use a newtype like NonEmptyName(String) with a fallible constructor that rejects empty/whitespace names, making invalid names unrepresentable

findings.problem: Function returns Vec<Record> instead of Result, hiding all parse failures
findings.failure_mode: Every malformed line silently panics rather than accumulating or returning typed errors; the caller cannot distinguish partial success from total failure
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, RecordParseError> where RecordParseError enumerates I/O and per-record parse failures

findings.problem: No try_reserve or capacity planning before Vec growth during collect
findings.failure_mode: Unbounded allocation growth per line; in pathological cases (many lines), memory exhaustion is possible without any reserve handling
findings.fix: If the line count is known, use Vec::with_capacity followed by try_reserve; at minimum, document the unbounded allocation risk

findings.problem: No benchmark exists to validate performance characteristics of load_sessions
findings.failure_mode: Allocation-heavy parsing path (split+collect per line, String allocations) is unmeasured; could regress with large inputs
findings.fix: Add a criterion or test-build benchmark for load_sessions with representative input sizes

findings.problem: No allocation profiling evidence for the parsing path
findings.failure_mode: Each line allocates a Vec<String> and multiple String values; total allocation count and bytes are unknown
findings.fix: Run with tracy, valgrind, or allocators-ignite to measure allocation count and bytes for representative inputs

findings.problem: No command evidence (cargo test, cargo fmt, cargo clippy) was produced
findings.failure_mode: Static review only; formatting violations, clippy lints, and test pass status are unverified
findings.fix: Run cargo fmt && cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, and cargo test in the task crate

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_sessions performance
no allocation profiling data for the parsing path
no cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy, or cargo test command evidence
no second-ring evidence (Miri, Kani, or proptest) for parse failure paths
residual_risk: Static review only; zero commands run. All I/O paths use unwrap/panic instead of typed errors. The core function mixes filesystem I/O with parsing, making it impure and untestable. Lossy as cast silently truncates u32 values. Multiple unchecked vector indices will panic on malformed input. Without running cargo test/clippy/fmt, formatting and lint status is unknown. The crate has no benchmarks, no allocation profiling, and no second-ring verification evidence.
